_comment: Severity and remediation are data so they can be tuned without touching the engine. Selectors are a deliberately small vocabulary: a general-purpose rule DSL here would be a bad programming language pretending to be configuration.

checks.title: Local device reaching its vendor's cloud
checks.detail: Home Assistant drives these locally, but the query log caught them contacting the vendor cloud on their own. This says who they spoke to, not what was said.
checks.remediation: Check the vendor's own app for a cloud service running in parallel, often called P2P, UID or remote access. Turning it off does not affect local control from Home Assistant.

checks.title: Device bypassing the resolver
checks.detail: Holds a DHCP lease but has never queried AdGuard: it uses a DNS server hardcoded in its firmware. Every DNS-based check is blind on this host.
checks.remediation: Set the network DNS on the device if it allows it. Otherwise redirect port 53 at the router. DNS over HTTPS stays out of reach either way.

checks.title: Integration not loaded
checks.detail: The config entry is not loaded, so its entities are unavailable right now. This is not an offline-resilience question: they are not working with or without an uplink. A stopped broker, a service that moved, or a failed migration all look like this.
checks.remediation: Open Settings, Devices and services and read the entry's error. If it points at a broker or a server, check that the service is actually running and that the address still matches: an add-on that was stopped or renamed is the common case.

checks.title: Third-party integration with cloud access
checks.detail: Integrations installed by hand or through HACS that talk to an external service. They are not reviewed by Home Assistant, and the credentials they hold pass through third-party code.
checks.remediation: Check that the repository is maintained and that installing it was your own decision. Not a flaw in itself: one more surface you are choosing to trust.

checks.title: Device talking outside from the trusted LAN
checks.detail: It sits on the network that also holds your computers and phones, and it reaches the outside on its own.
checks.remediation: Move it to the IoT VLAN if you have one. If you do not, this check is the best argument for building one.

checks.title: Cloud integration that has contacted nobody
checks.detail: Declared cloud by the manifest yet silent in the query log. Not a merit: either the device is not correlated, or it uses its own resolver, or the integration is not working.
checks.remediation: Check that the device is actually correlated to an IP and that the integration is loaded. A cloud that never speaks usually means something is wrong.

unverifiable.detail: Requires an attempt to connect to the broker without credentials. Talos has no MQTT client today: the check is not implemented, so it is neither passed nor failed.

checks.title: MQTT client matching no known asset

unverifiable.detail: Requires subscribing to $SYS/broker/clients/# and comparing against the registry. Source not implemented yet.
Requires security_class from the Z-Wave JS WebSocket. Source not implemented yet.
Requires knowing which ports devices speak on. DNS does not say, and a port scan is excluded by design. Only verifiable by reading the configuration of each video integration.

checks.title: Device in ARP absent from the Home Assistant registry

unverifiable.detail: Inside the Home Assistant container the ARP cache holds only the peers HA spoke to recently, not the whole LAN. DHCP leases remain the better source and already cover the case: see the zero check.
